description: Large-shape view of the CUDA public linalg API surface: the 82 cases whose largest matrix dimension is at least 256. `large` is a shape class, not a measured classification: no row is asserted to be compute- or bandwidth-bound, and a memory-bound row takes the same time here as at a small shape (`householder_r_default_f32` measured 34.698 µs at 512x256 and 35.223 µs at 64x32). These rows are never comparable with, or averaged together with, the per-call overhead rows of `gpu/linalg_public_api_latency` (tenferro-rs #2087). Rows here are lower than on pages published before this harness change because the harness used to open the CUDA engine once per case inside the timed region and now opens it once per arm, so the difference is removed harness cost and not a change in the kernels. The same problems, protocol and backends are split by shape class between the two suites. Issue 155.
